findings.title: Unhandled exception when get_user_info fails
findings.body: `get_user_info(payload["access_token"])` is called without any try/except. If the GitHub API request fails (network error, rate limit, invalid token, etc.), the exception propagates, resulting in a 500 error instead of the graceful error page returned by the `error` function. This can happen during routine outages or transient failures, breaking the installation flow for users. Wrap this call in a try/except and return `error(request, self.active_organization)` on failure.

findings.title: KeyError when integration metadata lacks 'sender'
findings.body: The code accesses `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` without checking that `"sender"` exists. Existing GitHub integrations created before this change may not have a `sender` field in their metadata, causing a KeyError and a 500 error during reinstallation for those users. Use a safe access like `integration.metadata.get("sender", {}).get("login")` or explicitly handle missing sender metadata (e.g., skip the check or fail with a clear message).

findings.title: Regression: block reinstallation when Integration is not ACTIVE
findings.body: The new query `Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id, status=ObjectStatus.ACTIVE)` and subsequent error return on DoesNotExist changes prior behavior. Previously, if an Integration existed with this external_id but was not linked to any OrganizationIntegration (e.g., after uninstall), the pipeline proceeded to `next_step()`. Now, if the Integration exists but its status is not ACTIVE (for example, DISABLED), the user receives an error and cannot complete installation. This can block legitimate reinstallation workflows where the Integration was disabled rather than deleted.
